subject: physics
question_text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of friction.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Advantages
lines: 2. Fingers can grip and hold objects.
4. Nails and screws hold in a wall.
steps.margin_note: Number them. Four or five one-line points read faster than a paragraph and are easier to mark.
steps.why: Every one of these is friction opposing a slip that would otherwise happen — the same mechanism, five settings.
common_mistakes: Writing one long paragraph, so the examiner has to hunt for the separate points.

recall.must_convey: At least two advantages of friction, such as walking, gripping, or braking.

steps.memory_tip: Remember five scenes: walking, gripping, braking, nails holding, belts driving — each one needs friction.

steps.margin_note: Two or three points are enough here. Do not pad the list once the marks are earned.
steps.why: All three are the same loss seen three ways: the work done against friction leaves the machine as heat.
common_mistakes: Repeating "wear and tear" in three different words as three separate points.

recall.must_convey: At least two disadvantages, such as wear and tear, heat, or loss of power.

steps.memory_tip: All three losses are one loss: work done against friction leaves as heat and wear.

insider_note: Two marks a side. Three numbered points each is full marks, and the disadvantages half is where students run short of examples.
